sentences: Computed on the binary32 word, with no float arithmetic.
A normal input has a biased exponent of 1..254.

`v_frexp_mant_f32` returns the input with its exponent set to 126 (a mantissa in [0.5, 1), sign kept); `v_frexp_exp_i32_f32` returns the biased exponent minus 126, so mantissa × 2^exponent is the input.
Zero and denormals (read as zero) give a signed zero and exponent 0; infinities and NaNs give the input unchanged and exponent 0.

`v_ldexp_f32` is S0 × 2^S1 with S1 a signed integer: S1 is clamped to [-512, 512] and added to the exponent field; a new field above 254 gives ±infinity, one of 0 or below gives ±0 (no denormal results), and zero, infinities and NaNs ignore S1.
Neg/abs, `clamp` and the output multipliers apply as for other float ops (not to the integer exponent result).

Source: the AMD [RDNA 2 ISA reference](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/radeon-tech-docs/instruction-set-architectures/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf) pseudocode for these three opcodes.

**Measured natively** on an RDNA2 iGPU (gfx1036, `tools/hw_oracle`): under the MODE inferred for the game (IEEE 0, f32 denormals flushed) the hardware gives the translator's word for all 30 special inputs of each frexp op and 741 ldexp cases (denormal inputs, results in and below the denormal range, every exponent clamp edge, NaN payloads).
With f32 denormals kept the hardware normalizes denormal inputs and returns denormal ldexp results, and with IEEE 1 it quiets signalling NaNs; neither is modelled, since the game runs with both off.
Checked on the CPU by `tests/semantic/test_alu_frexp_ldexp.py`; not run on the shader corpus.
